A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIDA/SID-Set research. The text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection, localization, robustness and ablation results in Tables 2–7, alongside qualitative outputs and appendix examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and appendix outputs, with revised detection scores in Tables 2 and 5.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Figure 5 retain the same detection and segmentation tokens, attention module, mask decoder, training stages and losses. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use SID-Set, MagicBrush and DMImage with the same detection, localization, explanation and image-perturbation coverage. The added DMImage sampling detail does not introduce another dataset or task.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain identical: eight detection baselines in Table 2, four localization baselines in Table 3 and six DMImage baselines in Table 5. Appendix comparisons also retain the same methods.

E3.justification: Previously stated splits, model sizes, training settings, metrics and perturbation procedures are retained. The class-averaging and balanced-DMImage statements disclose previously unspecified details of existing evaluations; they do not establish a revised experimental design or reruns.

E4.justification: The robustness tests in Table 4, attention and loss-weight ablations in Tables 6–7, and qualitative and failure analyses in Section 5.6 and Appendix C are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Table 2 parentheses continue to indicate fine-tuning score changes, not uncertainty.

E6.justification: Substantial aggregate-score revisions alter baseline gaps and trends in Tables 2 and 5. Table 2 changes LNP's overall F1 from 58.2 with a +4.1 fine-tuning change to 61.5 with a -10.4 change; SIDA-7B tampered accuracy changes from 91.2 to 92.7. Table 5 changes CNNSpot overall accuracy/F1 from 40.6/43.3 to 58.1/66.3 and SIDA-7B overall F1 from 92.4 to 92.0. These are revised reported results, not demonstrated gains from new experiments; nearly all per-class scores and other results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and their mathematical content are identical. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem or proof changes; the added averaging sentence explains metric reporting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: SID-Set and SIDA's combined detection, localization and explanation capabilities, with superior or comparable benchmark performance and generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of LGrad's errors and SIDA's localization behavior remain unchanged. The limitations concerning dataset size, reliance on FLUX and difficult tampering, including Appendix C's failure discussion, are retained.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly specifies that overall accuracy and F1 average the three categories. Table 5 newly states that equal numbers of real and fake DMImage images are sampled. Other implementation details, appendix prompts and resource-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 90 references and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix B are retained. Removing the access date from reference [31] is bibliographic editing, not a change in cited work.

P1.justification: Limited caption edits clarify Tables 2 and 5; the arXiv version/date text is updated and reference [31]'s access date is removed. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded captions cause modest table and text reflow, including repositioning Tables 6–7 and spilling the end of Appendix E onto a mostly empty page 12. All 19 figures and eight tables are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reporting clarity and numerical consistency by explaining aggregation and balanced sampling and revising discrepant overall scores. For example, CNNSpot's DMImage F1 changes from 43.3 to 66.3, matching the mean of its displayed class scores, 88.4 and 44.2. These are useful corrections within an otherwise unchanged study, with a small layout cost from the nearly empty appendix page.
